resource.description: This dataset contains MCAS results since 2017, including achievement level, participation rate, average scaled score, and average student growth percentile. The Massachusetts Comprehensive Assessment System (MCAS) is a statewide assessment administered to help parents, students, educators, and policymakers determine where districts, schools, and students are meeting expectations and where they need additional support. A new civics subject test has been administered since 2025. This dataset contains state, district and school results; MCAS results for collaboratives can be found in the Profiles report. A table documenting the transition from Legacy MCAS over time can be found in the DESE Researcher's Guide linked as featured content below. For more information about MCAS data, click here. Student growth percentile (AVG_SGP) was calculated as a median for 2017. In 2018 and onward, it is a mean. In 2021, a baseline SGP method was used to compare growth from 2019 to 2021, following the COVID-19 pandemic. For all other years, a cohort referenced model is used. For more information on SGP calculations, please see the Student Growth page on DESE's website. resource.name: Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs
resource.description:
This dataset includes monthly historic snapshots of programs licensed or funded by the Department of Early Education and Care (EEC). The data is pulled from EEC's Licensing Education Analytic Database (LEAD). For a list of current early education and care programs please visit the Current Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs dataset. Data are updated monthly at the beginning of each month.

Licensed programs are programs that are subject to licensing regulations by EEC, which include meeting health and safety standards, training and professional development requirements, criminal and background checks, and maintaining appropriate ratios of educators to children. Licensed programs can include any of the following: family child care and group and school age programs. For more information on licensed programs click here.

Funded programs are programs that are not subject to licensure by EEC but have the approval from EEC to provide subsidized child care for low-income or at-risk families. Funded programs can include any of the following: public schools; private schools; religious schools; and government, tribal, and military child care programs. For more information on funded providers click here.

The types of programs in this dataset include:

  • Licensed Family Child Care is child care provided in someone's home where the caretaker is not related to the children.

  • Licensed Center-Based Care, sometimes called group and school age programs, provide early education and care for young children in a non-residential setting such as a school or community center. These programs include several types of early education and care such as: Center-based care for infants, toddlers, preschool, or kindergarten age children; Early Head Start and Head Start programs; and Out-of- school time programs that operate before/after school or during the summer.

  • Funded Public Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and public schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all public schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten Enrollment dataset.

  • Funded Private Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and private schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all private schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Non-Public School Enrollment dataset.

resource.name: Public Postsecondary Tuition and Fees
resource.description: This dataset contains undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees for each public Massachusetts institution of higher education since fiscal year 2006 (FY06). Data are disaggregated by fiscal year, segment, institution, and student residency. These annual rates are based on full-time, undergraduate, state-supported tuition and mandatory fees, as published in the fall. This dataset contains two versions of tuition and mandatory fee data: 1) Nominal/Published Rates: the published tuition and fees for a given year, reflecting the actual cost at the time. 2) Inflation-Adjusted Rates: tuition and fees adjusted for inflation using 2024 dollars, to provide a consistent comparison of the cost of college over time. This dataset is 1 of 2 underlying datasets used in the interactive Tuition and Fees dashboard on the Department of Higher Education Data Center: 1) Public Postsecondary Tuition and Fees 2) Weighted Average Tuition and Fees by Public Postsecondary Segment Notes: - Data appear as reported to the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education. - Figures published by DHE may differ slightly from figures published by other institutions and organizations due to differences in timing of publication, data definitions, and calculation logic. - A fiscal year (FY) is 12-month period beginning July 1 and ending June 30. Because a fiscal year straddles two different calendar years, the calendar year and fiscal year will not always match. For example, FY 2025 runs from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. - Columns ADJ_TUITION_2024, ADJ_MAND_FEES_2024, and ADJ_TUITION_AND_MAND_FEES_2024 are adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Rates are converted to 2024 dollars to allow for consistence comparisons over time.

resource.name: MassCore Completion
resource.description: This report provides the number and percentage of Massachusetts public high school graduates who completed the MassCore recommended program of study each year since 2009. MassCore is a state-recommended program of study intended to align high school coursework with college and workforce expectations. The program of studies includes the successful completion of four units of English, four units of mathematics, three units of a lab-based science, three units of history, two units of the same world language, one unit of the arts, and five additional "core" courses. A computer science course that includes rigorous mathematical or scientific concepts and aligns with the 2016 Digital Literacy and Computer Science Framework can substitute for either a mathematics course or a laboratory science course. For more information on MassCore please click here. MassCore completion rates are not reported for any student group where the number graduated is less than 6. State graduation requirements changed between 2024 and 2025. This dataset reflects data for students submitted as graduates by their districts in the reporting year. resource.description: This dataset includes indicators that reflect attendance data for students in Massachusetts public schools since 2018. Because the information collected has changed over time, not all indicators are available across all years. Attendance indicators are calculated for students enrolled in grades PK-12 with at least 20 days in membership. For more information, please view the Profiles Help - About the Data page. Massachusetts defines chronically absent as missing at least 10 percent of days enrolled (for instance, 18 days absent if enrolled for a typical school year of 180 days), regardless of the reason for the absence. Being chronically absent can have a significant impact on a student's academic progress and their ability to access the variety of academic and non-academic supports that schools provide. Chronic absenteeism grew during the COVID-19 pandemic and, as of the 2022-23 school year, had not returned to pre-pandemic rates. For more information about chronic absence, visit the Chronic Absence and Student Attendance page. Economically Disadvantaged was used 2015-2021. resource.name: Current Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs
resource.description:
This dataset includes a snapshot of programs currently licensed or funded by the Department of Early Education and Care (EEC). The data is pulled from EEC's Licensing Education Analytic Database (LEAD). For a list of all current and historical early education and care programs please visit the Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs dataset. Data are updated monthly at the beginning of each month.

Licensed programs are programs that are subject to licensing regulations by EEC, which include meeting health and safety standards, training and professional development requirements, criminal and background checks, and maintaining appropriate ratios of educators to children. Licensed programs can include any of the following: family child care and group and school age programs. For more information on licensed programs click here.

Funded programs are programs that are not subject to licensure by EEC but have the approval from EEC to provide subsidized child care for low-income or at-risk families. Funded programs can include any of the following: public schools; private schools; religious schools; and government, tribal, and military child care programs. For more information on funded providers click here.

The types of programs in this dataset include:

  • Licensed Family Child Care is child care provided in someone's home where the caretaker is not related to the children.

  • Licensed Center-Based Care, sometimes called group and school age programs, provide early education and care for young children in a non-residential setting such as a school or community center. These programs include several types of early education and care such as: Center-based care for infants, toddlers, preschool, or kindergarten age children; Early Head Start and Head Start programs; and Out-of- school time programs that operate before/after school or during the summer.

  • Funded Public Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and public schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all public schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten Enrollment dataset.

  • Funded Private Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and private schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all private schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Non-Public School Enrollment dataset.

resource.description: This dataset contains the total annual unduplicated headcount and share of enrollment for undergraduate and graduate students in credit-bearing courses at public community colleges and state universities in Massachusetts since 2014. Data are disaggregated by fiscal year, segment, institution, and enrollment level, reporting counts and percentages of total enrollment by gender, race/ethnicity, residency, and age. This dataset is 1 of 2 datasets that is also published in the interactive Annual Enrollment dashboard on the Department of Higher Education Data Center: 1) Public Postsecondary Annual Enrollment: Detail 2) Public Postsecondary Annual Enrollment: Summary Related datasets: 1) Public Postsecondary Fall Enrollment 2) Public Postsecondary Fall Enrollment by Race and Gender Notes: - Data appear as reported to the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education. - Annual enrollment refers to a 12 month enrollment period over one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). - Figures published by DHE may differ slightly from figures published by other institutions and organizations due to differences in timing of publication, data definitions, and calculation logic. - Data for the University of Massachusetts are not included due to unique reporting requirements. See Fall Enrollment for HEIRS data on UMass enrollment. -The most common measure of enrollment is headcount of enrolled students. Annual headcount enrollment is unduplicated, meaning any individual student is only counted once per institution and fiscal year, even if they are enrolled in multiple terms. Enrollment can also be measured as full-time equivalent (FTE) students, a calculation based on the sum of credits carried by all enrolled students. In a fiscal year, 30 undergraduate credits = 1 undergraduate FTE, and 24 graduate credits = 1 graduate FTE at a state university.

For details on the process and suppression rules, please visit the Employment and Earnings of High School Graduates dashboard. This dataset is one of three containing the same data that is also published in the Employment and Earnings of High School Graduates dashboard: Average Earnings by Student Group Average Earnings by Industry College and Career Outcomes 2025 Update on DESE Data on Employment and Earnings  The data link between high school graduates and future earnings makes it possible to follow students beyond high school and college into the workforce, enabling long-term evaluation of educational programs using workforce outcomes. While DESE has published these data in the past, as of June 2025 we are temporarily pausing updates due to an issue conducting the link that was brought to our attention in 2023 by a team of researchers. The issue impacts the earnings information for students who never attended a postsecondary institution or who only attended private or out-of-state colleges or universities, beginning with the 2017 high school graduation cohort, with growing impact in each successive high school graduation cohort. The issue does not impact the earnings information for students who attended a Massachusetts public institution of higher education, and earnings data for those students will continue to be updated. Once a solution is found, the past cohorts of data with low match rates will be updated. DESE and partner agencies are exploring linking strategies to maximize the utility of the information. More detailed information can be found in the attached memo provided by the research team from the Annenberg Institute. We thank them for calling this issue to our attention.

resource.name: High School Graduates Attending Higher Education
resource.description: This dataset provides information about Massachusetts public high school graduates enrolling into institutions of higher education by student group since 2004. resource.name: Chart: Chronic Absenteeism by Student Group
resource.description: This report includes several indicators that reflect attendance information collected on March 1st and at the end of the selected school year for students in grades PK-12. Attendance rate indicates the average percentage of days in attendance for students enrolled in grades PK - 12 with at least 20 days in membership. Massachusetts defines chronically absent as missing at least 10 percent of days enrolled (for instance, 18 days absent if enrolled for a typical school year of 180 days), regardless of the reason for the absence. Being chronically absent can have a significant impact on a student's academic progress and their ability to access the variety of academic and non-academic supports that schools provide. Chronic absenteeism grew during the COVID-19 pandemic and, as of the 2022-23 school year, had not returned to pre-pandemic rates. Almost 1 in 4 Massachusetts students missed 18 or more days of school in 2022-23. To see which schools were identified as Attendance Priority Schools in fall 2023, download this file: Attendance Priority Schools.

resource.name: Early College Credits
resource.description: This dataset contains data on credits registered and earned by students in designated Early College programs since school year 2021-22. Early College is a program that designates partnerships between high schools and colleges to support high school students to complete college courses. The list of designated partnerships is available here. Students are counted in this dataset if they are marked as an Early College student by the district. Credits are counted in this dataset if they are submitted to DHE. The credits are counted based on where they are taken, even if that is an institution of higher ed (IHE) outside of the student's designated Early College partnership. Credits from Fall and Spring semester are counted; summer credits are not counted. Data includes any credits at public IHEs (Wentworth Institute of Technology data have not been submitted as of July 2024), and '22-23 data from private IHEs that are part of an Early College designated partnership. The dataset is updated in the fall of each year to add in the previous year's credits. Credit counts are suppressed (hidden) for groups in which there are fewer than 6 students to protect student privacy, though those credits are still counted in totals. The data here are the same as the credit data in the MA Early College Dashboard.

The FTE column is for display only.

resource.name: Public Postsecondary First-Year Retention and Persistence: Summary
resource.description: This dataset contains first-year retention and persistence rates and counts (Fall to Fall) for first-time and new transfer, degree-seeking undergraduate students. It covers all public community colleges and state universities in Massachusetts, and the University of Massachusetts since 2013. Data are disaggregated by report year, cohort year, segment, institution, student type, and enrollment status/intensity. This dataset is 1 of 3 underlying datasets used in the interactive First-Year Retention and Persistence dashboard on the Department of Higher Education Data Center: 1) Public Postsecondary First-Year Retention and Persistence: Summary 2) Public Postsecondary First-Year Retention and Persistence by Race/Ethnicity 3) Public Postsecondary First-Year Retention and Persistence by Gender Definitions: - Cohort Identification: Students are included in the cohort if their first fall term meets the following criteria: new first-time or new transfer, degree-seeking, and enrolled full-time (12+ credits) or part-time. - Adjusted Cohort Count (Retention): Number of first-year students in the cohort, excluding those who completed a credential within the first year. - Adjusted Cohort Count (Persistence): Number of first-year students in the cohort who can be tracked across institutions, excluding those who earned a credential within their first year. - Retained: A student who enrolled in their first fall semester and returned the following fall at their initial institution. - Persisted: A student who enrolled in their first fall semester and returned the following fall at any institution in the U.S. (including transfer to another institution). This is identified using Massachusetts Department of Higher Education data or National Student Clearinghouse (NSC) data. Why do cohort counts differ? Persistence measures require students to be trackable across institutions to determine whether they enrolled at another college or university in a later term. Students who cannot be tracked for this purpose are excluded from Persistence cohorts but remain included in Retention cohorts. Notes: - To comply with data privacy laws, outcomes for student groups with cohort sizes <= 6 are suppressed. - Figures published by DHE may differ slightly from figures published by other institutions and organizations due to differences in timing of publication, data definitions, and calculation logic. - Figures in this dashboard may also differ from other DHE analyses and reports that use a broader cohort to calculate retention, i.e., including part-time and/or new transfer students.

resource.name: Children Enrolled in Formal Early Education and Care Statewide
resource.description: This dataset includes the estimated number of children statewide and by region using data from the US Census, as well as the subset of children estimated to be enrolled in formal early education and care programs across the mixed delivery system. Additionally, the dataset includes the total number of children in families with household income below 50% of the state median income and whether all adults in the household are in the labor force, based on data from the US Census, along with the number of children who receive Child Care Financial Assistance (CCFA). This dataset comes from the Child Universal Success Platform (CUSP), an integrated data system developed by Third Sector Intelligence (3Si) in partnership with the Department of Early Education and Care (EEC). resource.name: Crosswalk of Career Technical Education (CTE) Programs to Occupations
resource.description:
This crosswalk maps Massachusetts' Career Technical Education (CTE) pathway programs to aligned occupations. These are defined as occupations that enrolled students are typically prepared to enter upon graduation given the skills and knowledge covered in the program, without any subsequent schooling. The crosswalk was created jointly by the Department of Economic Research (DER) at the Executive Office of Labor and Workforce Development (EOLWD) and the Office of College, Career, and Technical Education at the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE). It matches active CTE program codes found in the Student Information Management System (SIMS) Data Handbook Appendices with occupations in the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) system. Mappings were determined based on standard curriculum described in the CTE Instructional Frameworks as well as occupational requirements observed in recent labor market data. Please note that not all program codes in the SIMS Data Handbook are represented; programs were excluded if no aligned entry-level occupation could be identified, if no graduates had been produced, or if no active programs existed in the state at the time the crosswalk was created. Additional versions of this crosswalk will be created as program curriculum or the labor market changes, when there are changes to the SIMS or SOC coding systems, or as currently excluded programs produce graduates, establish active programs, and develop occupational alignments. Data used to create this crosswalk:
  • SIMS Data Handbook Appendices v1.1 (2025-2026 school year)
  • CTE Instructional Frameworks as of March 2026
  • 2018 SOC system from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (detailed 6-digit codes used, except in cases where labor market information was published in 2023 for aggregated codes)
  • Labor market data from the American Community Survey 5-year (2018-2023) and Lightcast job postings (2025)
For more information on the SOC system or how to use labor market information, please contact economicresearch@mass.gov.

resource.name: Special Education Circuit Breaker Reimbursements
resource.description:
This dataset includes reimbursement amounts provided to Massachusetts public school districts through the Commonwealth's Special Education Circuit Breaker program ("circuit breaker") starting with fiscal year 2006. It also includes expenditure amounts reported to the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) on annual circuit breaker claims. Circuit breaker program reimburses districts for qualified high-cost special education expenditures in two categories: instruction/tuition and transportation. Instruction/tuition has been reimbursed since the program’s inception. Transportation reimbursement was added with the Student Opportunity Act (beginning fiscal year 2022). Districts report costs annually through a claiming process. Expenses over the annual per-student claim threshold are reimbursed quarterly, in the following fiscal year, and at a consistent percentage statewide dependent on available budget. Per statute (M.G.L. Chapter 71B Section 5A), reimbursements are calculated first in the instruction/tuition category. Then, any money left in the state circuit breaker budget line is calculated for transportation reimbursement. Additionally, each year the per-student claim threshold increases based on inflation according to a defined formula. Circuit breaker reimburses through multiple program components:
  • Quarterly payments are provided four times per year and are reimbursements for expenses incurred in the prior fiscal year. Expenses in the instruction and tuition category have been reimbursed since the program's inception. Beginning with the implementation of the Student Opportunity Act (FY22 payments), expenses for out-of-district transportation are also reimbursed.
  • Extraordinary Relief payments are provided once a year to districts showing a significant (greater than 25%) increase in instruction and tuition expenses over the prior year. This reimbursement is provided to qualified districts in the same fiscal year expenses were incurred.
  • Additional/Supplemental payments are provided in atypical scenarios, such as in years when the legislature enacts additional circuit breaker reimbursement mechanisms or authorizes supplemental funding for distribution.
More information regarding the circuit breaker program can be found on the DESE circuit breaker website, including historic information of claim thresholds and percentage reimbursement rates. In addition to the standard reimbursement percentages indicated in the chart, students claimed with special indicators (homeless, state ward or abandoned) are reimbursed at 100% over the claim threshold.

resource.name: Elementary and Secondary District Expenditures Per Pupil
resource.description:
This dataset contains per-pupil expenditure data for Massachusetts public school districts from 2009 onward. Per-pupil expenditure data for charter schools can be found in the Massachusetts Charter School Financial Dashboard. Districts report expenditure data via the End of Year Financial Report. Per-pupil expenditures are calculated by dividing a district’s operating expenditures by its average pupil membership. Measures include both in-district expenditures per pupil and total expenditures per pupil. The following data elements are used in these calculations:
  • In-District Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) Average Membership: Average enrollment across the school year for pupils enrolled in district schools.
  • In-District Expenditures: All district operating expenditures for in-district programs.
  • In-District Expenditures Per Pupil: Total in-district expenditures divided by in-district FTE average membership.
  • Total FTE Average Membership: Average enrollment across the school year for students enrolled in district schools as well as publicly funded students enrolled in other placements, including charter schools, special education collaboratives, and private special education schools.
  • Total Expenditures: All district operating expenditures, including both in-district programs and out-of-district placements.
  • Total Expenditures Per Pupil: Total expenditures divided by total FTE average membership.
This dataset contains a subset of the data also published in the School Finance Dashboard. For more information about the dashboard and its corresponding datasets, see the School Finance Dashboard landing page in the E2C Hub. Amendments to district expenditures or FTE counts are included in this dataset, meaning data may be updated over time. Per pupil expenditure data is also published on our DESE Profiles site but may differ slightly due to timing of amendments and rounding: Per Pupil Expenditure

resource.name: Weighted Average Tuition and Fees by Public Postsecondary Segment
resource.description: This dataset contains average undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees rates weighted by enrollment for each public Massachusetts segment of higher education since fiscal year 2006 (FY06). Data are disaggregated by fiscal year, segment, and student residency. Annual rates are based on full-time, undergraduate, state-supported tuition and mandatory fees, as published in the fall. Segment-level averages are weighted by each segment's share of undergraduate full-time equivalent (FTE) enrollment. This dataset contains two versions of weighted tuition and mandatory fee data: 1) Nominal/Published Rates: the weighted average cost of tuition and mandatory fees for a given year at a given higher education segment, reflecting the actual cost at the time. 2) Inflation-Adjusted Rates: the weighted average cost of tuition and mandatory fees adjusted for inflation using 2024 dollars, to provide a consistent comparison of the cost of attending a higher education segment over time. This dataset is 1 of 2 underlying datasets used in the interactive Tuition and Fees dashboard on the Department of Higher Education Data Center: 1) Public Postsecondary Tuition and Fees 2) Weighted Average Tuition and Fees by Public Postsecondary Segment Notes: - Data appear as reported to the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education. - Figures published by DHE may differ slightly from figures published by other institutions and organizations due to differences in timing of publication, data definitions, and calculation logic. - A fiscal year (FY) is 12-month period beginning July 1 and ending June 30. Because a fiscal year straddles two different calendar years, the calendar year and fiscal year will not always match. For example, FY 2025 runs from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. - Weights are calculated using the percentage of undergraduate FTE of the total segment and the total FTE of the previous fiscal year. FTE figures from the previous fiscal year are used due to reporting schedules. - Inflation-adjusted columns (ADJ_WEIGHTED_AVG_*) are adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Rates are converted to 2024 dollars to allow for consistence comparisons over time.

resource.name: College-Going Trends In State vs. Out of State
resource.description: This dataset provides information about Massachusetts public high school graduates enrolling into institutions of higher education by student group since 2004. It includes the count and percentage of students enrolled in any college or university, as well as a breakdown of enrollment in private vs. public, two-year vs. four-year, and Massachusetts vs. out-of-state institutions. It also includes the percentage of students enrolled in a Massachusetts community college, a Massachusetts state university, or the University of Massachusetts system. The data provided in the report are based on point-in-time matching of graduates with higher education enrollment data from the National Student Clearinghouse (NSC). For more information about working with NSC data, including coverage and FERPA implications, please visit their Working with Our Data page. Results are not reported for higher education enrollments of fewer than 15. Prior to the 2015 high school graduating class, the data refers to students attending college within 16 months of graduating high school. From 2015 on, the data is also provided by high school graduates attending college by the March following their high school graduation year. The percentages in the report are available by college attendee or high school graduate. Economically Disadvantaged was used 2015-2021. Low Income was used prior to 2015, and a different version of Low Income has been used since 2022. Please see the DESE Researcher's Guide for more information. State graduation requirements changed between 2024 and 2025. This dataset reflects data for students submitted as graduates by their districts in the reporting year. This dataset contains the same data that is also published on our DESE Profiles site: Graduates Attending Higher Ed
